title: Protecting Your Identity
drDigitalIntro:
Identity theft is when someone uses your personal information to pretend to be you — to open bank accounts, make purchases, or access your accounts.
• Never share your national ID, passport number, or full bank details online unless required by a trusted official site.
• Use strong passwords (see Unit 10, Passwords) and two-factor authentication for banking and email.
• Watch your bank statements for unfamiliar charges — that is often the first warning sign.
• You can limit how much websites track you by adjusting your browser privacy settings.
• If identity theft happens: contact your bank immediately, change your passwords, and report it to your consumer protection agency.

playgroundTask.goal: Tighten your privacy settings to reduce tracking

steps.say: Click Privacy in the Settings sidebar.
Turn off Cross-Site Tracking — this stops websites following you across the web.
Turn off Location Sharing so websites cannot see where you are.

drDigitalSuccess: Your privacy settings are tighter! Turning off tracking makes it harder for data collectors to build a profile about you.
drDigitalHint: Open Privacy in the Settings sidebar, then click the toggles to turn off Cross-Site Tracking and Location Sharing.
